latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The evaluation kept the correct counts for one lion, seven raccoons, and one croissant, and the raccoons were correctly placed to the left of the croissant. However, the lion was not recognized as checkered, the lion was not clearly chasing the raccoons, raccoon presence was weak despite the count passing, and the croissant was not recognized as stone. The next prompt should make the scene read as a simple side-view chase with the lion behind the raccoons, make all seven raccoons individually recognizable and unobstructed, and bind the checkered pattern to the lion and the stone material to the croissant with more explicit visual cues.
expected_improvement: The lion should be recognized as checkered because the prompt requires a bold, visible checkered pattern covering only the lion.
The chase relation should be clearer because the lion is placed directly behind the seven raccoons in a side-view running layout, facing and pursuing them.
The raccoons should be more reliably detected because all seven are requested as separate, complete, recognizable raccoons with clear silhouettes.
The croissant should be recognized as stone because it is described as a croissant-shaped object carved from rough stone, with visible rock texture.
preserve_constraints: Keep exactly seven raccoons visible and countable.
Keep all seven raccoons to the left of the single croissant.
Do not include any extra lions, raccoons, or croissants.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt mentioned the required attributes and chase relation, but it did not enforce a simple unambiguous side-view pursuit layout or strong enough visual attribute cues. The checkered pattern may have been too subtle or not bound to the lion, the stone material may have appeared like an ordinary croissant, and the raccoons may not have been distinct enough for object recognition.
previous_plan_error.error_source: Weak attribute binding and weak action/layout specification in the initial prompt.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple left-to-right composition: one checkered lion on the far left, seven raccoons in the middle-left running away from it, and one stone croissant on the far right. Make the lion visibly pursuing the raccoons, keep all raccoons separate and recognizable, and make the croissant clearly a carved stone croissant rather than a normal pastry.
regression_risks: The generator may lose the exact count of seven raccoons if they overlap or merge.
The generator may add extra animals while depicting a chase.
The generator may make the croissant look like a normal pastry instead of stone.
The generator may apply the checkered pattern to the background or other objects instead of only the lion.
repair_constraints: Make the single lion visibly checkered, with a bold checkered pattern on the lion's body only.
Show the single lion actively chasing the seven raccoons: the lion must be behind the raccoons, facing them, running toward them, while the raccoons run away from the lion.
Make all seven raccoons clearly present as separate, complete, recognizable raccoons, with no merged bodies and no hidden individuals.
Make the single croissant visibly stone: a croissant-shaped object carved from rough stone, with clear rock texture, not a soft pastry.
latest_teacher_action.retry_prompt: A clear side-view scene with exactly one lion, exactly seven raccoons, and exactly one croissant. On the far left, show the one lion running to the right and chasing the raccoons; the lion's body is covered with a bold, unmistakable checkered pattern, and the checkered pattern belongs only to the lion. In the middle-left, show seven separate, complete, recognizable raccoons running away from the lion, all fully visible, not overlapping, not merged, and easy to count as exactly seven. On the far right, place exactly one croissant-shaped object made of rough stone, visibly carved from stone with rock texture. All seven raccoons must be to the left of the stone croissant. Keep the lion behind the raccoons and facing them so the chase is obvious. Do not include any extra lions, raccoons, or croissants.
